messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-4821 — GPU memory pressure detected in cluster gpu-prod-east-2. Threshold: gpu.mem.used > 92% for 90s. Affected nodes: gpu-n1,gpu-n3. Autopager: true. Link: https://pd.example/PD-4821

pagerduty: Incident PD-4821 triggered by metric alert (gpu.mem.pressure). Paging oncall: @sara

sara (oncall): ack via PD. I'm on it — starting triage now.

sara (oncall): quick check of node metrics: gpu-n1 at 96% mem, gpu-n3 at 91%. I see repeated OOMKilled events for pod model-infer-12 (2x).

matt: pulling the pod logs and ksvc traces. Visible spike at ~14:01 UTC in KV cache evictions (prefetch eviction rate x6). Suspect a prefetch/batch job storm.

liam: tagging customer-impact: some clients in eu-west-2 got 503s between 14:01-14:06 UTC. Can we quantify? @matt

matt: confirmed ~0.7% of requests in region, request ids sample: req_8a3f1c, req_bb9d2f. Clients retried; no persisted data lost but latency/regrets.

sara (oncall): mitigation plan (short):
- cordon gpu-n1 and evict non-critical batch pods
- scale up nodegroup with +2 smaller GPU nodes to increase headroom
- push routing fallback: route 5% of traffic to cpu-quantized model variant to reduce peak VRAM

sara (oncall): running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-n1
kubectl drain gpu-n1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Evicting batch jobs...

ops-bot: Autoscaler: nodegroup gpu-prod-east-2 scaled from 6 -> 8 (requested at 2026-02-22T14:03:12Z). New nodes expected ~90s.

matt: pushed routing change: canary 5% -> cpu-quantized fallback. Monitoring KV eviction rates. Early signs: eviction rate halving.

sara (oncall): GPU mem usage on gpu-n1 dropping 96% -> 78% after evictions and canary traffic. Holding mitigation for 10m while monitoring.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-4821 acknowledged by sara at 2026-02-22T14:10:12Z

liam: @customer-success-bot can you draft a short customer blurb for CS/ops? Need to advise affected customers.

customer-success-bot: Draft message: "We experienced a brief service degradation in our eu-west region between 14:01-14:06 UTC causing some requests to return 503. Mitigation has been applied; we're investigating the root cause and will follow up. No customer data was lost." :white_check_mark:

matt: uploading aggregated logs + traces to incident bucket: s3://incidents/PD-4821/logs.tar.gz. Also captured KV cache histograms and prefetch traces.

sara (oncall): handing off to night oncall in ~15m. I'll leave a short runbook:
- cause: prefetch storm from batch job increased KV evictions -> pressure on GPU memory due to hot embeddings + large batch sizes
- immediate mitigation: cordon/evict, scale nodegroup, route fallback to cpu-quantized
- followups: add prefetch backoff on batch jobs, increase autoscale headroom, adjust alert thresholds for sustained vs transient spikes

liam: taking over. Summary for handoff: autoscale + canary fallback mitigated the immediate pressure, no ongoing 503s after 14:12 UTC. Follow-ups: open RFC to add prefetch backoff and re-evaluate P1 alert thresholds.

sara (oncall): changing status in incident tracker to 'monitoring' and leaving for postmortem if we observe recurrence.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-4821 status updated to 'monitoring' by sara

matt: note — found one batch job launched with 3x configured shards (operator error). Owner: @data-batch-team. That explains the sudden high prefetch concurrency.

liam: pinging @data-batch-team to schedule a fix and add a guardrail in job submission. I'll open a follow-up ticket.

sara (oncall): last sanity check: no further OOMs or 5xx spikes in last 7m. Leaving thread for postmortem artifacts.

matt: linking logs & perf dump: https://internal.storage/incidents/PD-4821/

liam: noted. Closing active paging; moving to follow-ups.

sara (oncall): resolved->monitoring. Hand-off complete. Thanks all. :shipit:
